primary.semantic: read u8 selector, double modulo 256, patch E688 and jump through D100+2*(selector&7F)
primary.notes: All selectors mapped without executing their targets; only the first 41 cells are directory-shaped. Service semantics are a separate layer.

primary.semantic: pop condition; branch when bit 0 is clear, otherwise advance 2
primary.operands: u8 b: if b<0x80 target=PC+2+b; otherwise cell=word(0x54)+b-256, target=cell-word(cell), all modulo 65536
primary.notes: Only low-word bit 0 is tested; nonzero even values also branch. Table read is skipped when bit 0 is set.

primary.semantic: replace pointer by pointer+2*index, modulo 65536
primary.notes: No frame/header bias; distinct from local/global indexed access.

primary.semantic: replace pointer by word at pointer+2*index, modulo 65536
primary.notes: No frame/header bias; distinct from local/global indexed access.

primary.semantic: pop index and base, push base+2*stride*index modulo 65536
primary.notes: Stride 1 has a shift fast path; other values use native multiply helper. No runtime bounds established.

primary.semantic: address word/address at frame + 10 + 2*index; base $50/$51
primary.notes: D155 scales the index and advances the pointer an extra byte in the long form. Non-minimal two-byte form is accepted.

primary.semantic: push address of length byte and skip inline byte payload
primary.operands: u8 length followed by length bytes
primary.notes: No assumption about text encoding or payload data type.

primary.semantic: address at word(BD9E+2*(selector&7F)) + 2*index, modulo 65536

primary.semantic: pop source then destination; copy 2*count bytes in increasing address order
primary.notes: Not overlap-safe memmove. Zero count and 256/512-byte boundaries checked; larger counts not exhaustively replayed.

primary.semantic: load word/address at frame + 10 + 2*index; base $50/$51
primary.notes: D155 scales the index and advances the pointer an extra byte in the long form. Non-minimal two-byte form is accepted.

primary.semantic: pop source then destination; copy length-prefixed string subject to u8 capacity
primary.notes: A source word with zero high byte is a single character; excess length enters error 113.

primary.semantic: store word/address at frame + 10 + 2*index; base $50/$51
primary.notes: D155 scales the index and advances the pointer an extra byte in the long form. Non-minimal two-byte form is accepted.

primary.semantic: pop signed selector, align PC with OR 1; inclusive bounds select backward self-relative target, else continue at aligned PC+5
primary.operands: alignment-dependent signed lower/upper words; branch cells start aligned PC+7
primary.notes: Target cell is aligned PC+7+2*(value-lower), target=cell-word(cell).

primary.semantic: restore native SP from frame+10, push result words, restore allocation/local/branch/segment/PC context
primary.notes: Results start frame+12, copied so the first result is on top. Different first-byte segment identifiers invoke E646 before final restoration; high-count Y wrapping is raw native behavior, not a validated language range.

primary.semantic: call current segment procedure; search dynamic chain by lexical level then select its predecessor
primary.notes: Parameters/locals determine allocation; native procedures bypass frame allocation. Nonresident segment I/O remains an explicit service boundary.

primary.semantic: pop index and base, push zero-extended byte at (base+index)&FFFF

primary.semantic: pop value, index, base; store low byte at (base+index)&FFFF

primary.semantic: replace base/index by base+2*(abs(signed index) div count), width, and duplicated low byte of magnitude remainder*width

limitations: Initial interpreter-ready snapshot only; future table or code modifications are not modeled.
No decimal arithmetic, V flag branches, ROM, devices, cycles, interrupts or complete CPU implementation.
Unsupported native instructions and excessive steps fail explicitly.
Sampled word values and page-boundary cases are checks, not exhaustive mathematical proof.
No p-code file or instruction-stream disassembler is implemented.
